First case: the student poses a risk to themselves or others. Second case: the occurrence of sexual harassment against children.

Counseling and wellbeing > How many and the necessary duration of meetings?
The number of sessions depends on the student's goals and what she/he want to achieve, where the total is between 6 to 8 sessions. The duration of each session 45 minutes to 60 minutes.

The change process is not immediate but need time, effort, inner desire, determination, and persistence, so you should start with a practical plan for change and seek to implement them and modify them to suit the student to note the change. No. Counseling and Wellbeing Service is obliged to confidentiality of all student data and not share it outside of the center except in cases requiring it in advance and written approval of student knowledge. Where the requesting service center after 4-5 years to destroy the file.

Overview


Services
Our friendly and confidential support and advice are available to current students with disabilities who are registered at the University as well as to faculty/staff dealing with such students. The different support options available vary according to the specific requirements of the student with a disability.

Students of Determination Services office works in partnership with faculty and staff in UAEU academic departments and other university services to provide different types of support for students with disabilities.

Support services include:

Review written documentation of the functional limitations and associated educational recommendations for each student.

Prepare an Individual Accommodation Plan or IAP summarizing the appropriate educational accommodations.

Help disabled students understand the academic support that is available and signpost other available services they may wish to access.

Refer students to other UAEU resources as needed.

Assist in arranging needed course, classroom, and testing adjustments; and facilitate the provision of recommended adjustments.

Arrange exam proctoring that requires specialized equipment such as the Kurzweil Reader software.

Liaise and coordinate with faculty/staff and other departments working with disabled students to discuss potential adjustment solutions including adaptive technology equipment options.

Support students’ learning strategies and enhance students’ self-reliance and independence.

Provide students with assistive adaptive technology devices on loan bases.

Administer training for students with disabilities, faculty and staff in the use of specific adaptive technology.

Provide a computer lab for students with disabilities.

Provide students with a cost-effective and timely production of print materials in alternative reading formats (i.e., Braille, audio texts, etc).

Advocate for campus accessibility for all persons with disability at UAEU including students, staff and faculty.

Develop collaborative opportunities with other UAEU academic departments and external funding bodies.

Frequently Asked Questions


Frequently Asked Questions > Library Deanship


Frequently Asked Questions > What are the Library’s open hours?
Library hours depend on time of the year, such as Regular Semester, Summer Semester, Ramadan, etc. It is best to see the current hours in our library hour’s .

Frequently Asked Questions > Can the general community (non-UAEU) use the library?
Yes, the general community (non-UAEU) may use the library during appropriate male/female timings . If you wish to borrow any books, you can apply for Community User Membership, which requires a deposit and registration fee.

For more information, please contact the Circulation staff at circ_lib@uaeu.ac.ae or by telephone at 03 713 4684 , 03 713 4671

Frequently Asked Questions > How many books may I check out?
Depending on user type, you may borrow up to the following number of general books with varying loan periods. Please note that Special Collections, Reserves, and Multimedia may have different borrowing rules or restrictions.

USER | NO. OF ITEMS | LOAN PERIOD | RENEW BOOKS
UAEU Bachelor Student/Master | 10 | 30 days 14 days (Emirates books) | General books (2 times) Emirates Books (2 time)
UAEU PhD Student | 20 | 120 days 14 days (Emirates books) | General books (2 times) Emirates Books (2 time)
UAEU Faculty Member | 20 | 120 days 14 Days (Emirates books) | General books (2 times) Emirates Books (2 time)
UAEU Staff Member | 10 | 30 days 14 Days (Emirates books) | General books (2 times) Emirates Books (2 time)
Community User | 10 | 30 days 14 days (Emirates books) | General books (2 times) Emirates Books (2 time)

Frequently Asked Questions > How do I renew books?
There are a number of ways you can renew your books:

Online at the Login page https://authn.sd02.worldcat.org/wayf/metaauth-ui/cmnd/protocol/samlpost

By email request at: circ_lib@uaeu.ac.ae

By telephone at 03-713-4684 -(4677) -(4671)

In person at any lending desk or self-check Machine.

Frequently Asked Questions > How do I get clearance from the library?
You should first make sure your library record is clear (all books returned, and any fines/fees are paid) by contacting the Lending Desk staff:

By email request at: circ_lib@uaeu.ac.ae

Onsite at the Lending Desk

By telephone at 03 713 4684 - 4677- 4671

In person at any lending desk

Frequently Asked Questions > How much money do I owe in library fines or fees?
The amount depends on whether or not you have overdue books that have accrued fines, and replacement and/or processing fees for lost or missing books.

Usually, you will receive email notification for any overdue books or fees, but please check with the Lending Desk staff to confirm your fees at circ_lib@uaeu.ac.ae or by telephone at 03 713 4684 - 4677- 4671.

Frequently Asked Questions > How can I pay my fines?
Please contact the Lending Desk staff by email at circ_lib@uaeu.ac.ae or by telephone at 03 713 4684 - 4677 - 4671 to confirm the exact amount that you owe. Then, you can pay by using one of the following methods.

If you have a Visa or MasterCard, you can pay directly at the lending Desk.

Alternatively, you may deposit the amount into the Library Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank account (# 11447524920001), and obtain a receipt. You can then either:

send the original bank deposit receipt via email circ_lib@uaeu.ac.ae ,

Or bring it in person to the library service desk.

Frequently Asked Questions > How do I find a book in the library?
You can search for a book using the library’s online catalog at:

https://uaeu.on.worldcat.org/advancedsearch?queryString=&spellcheck=true , Once you find the book, note the call number, which tells you where to find it on the shelf.

Frequently Asked Questions > Where is the Library located?
The Main Library is located at UAEU in Building D2. Access is via the basement of the Crescent Building.

Frequently Asked Questions > If I am not a member of UAEU, may I still access your e-resources?
Yes, e-resources are available for the non-member physically present in the library.

Frequently Asked Questions > I can’t access the e-resources, even though I entered my username and password. What do I need to do?
Please make sure that you are using the correct email username (without the extension "@uaeu.ac.ae") and your password.

Make sure you are accessing the e-resources from our website or try clearing your browser history.

Or request the assistance via e-mail: digital.library@uaeu.ac.ae

Frequently Asked Questions > Can the libraries provide assistance with publishing my research?
Yes, the Libraries offer support for free for faculty, students and staff with: literature reviews (including systematic reviews); accessing documents and papers from other institutions; selection of journals for publication; manuscript editing; and support for publishing with commercial publishers or publishing via the UAEU institutional repository as open access material. Or you can contact Dr. (Shahab Majoud) via e-mail: Smajud@uaeu.ac.ae

Frequently Asked Questions > Tipasa Interlibrary Loan of books for LIWA Consortium
Who can request and borrow via LIWA Tipasa?

Registered students, staff and faculty of UAEU.

How many items can be requested?

A patron can borrow maximum of 10 items for faculty member, students and staff per visit.

For how long can an item be borrowed?

LIWA Tipasa's item can be borrowed for one month for all faculty member, students and staff. The item can be renewed for two times.

What happens if the book is returned late?

Overdue notices will be sent to the patron as a reminder to return the book.

What happens if an item is lost?

Patrons will be required to pay for replacement of lost or damaged items at their local library. A default fee is DHS100 will be added to the price of the lost or damaged item.

What can be borrowed?

All items can be borrowed except for non-circulating items e.g., multimedia materials and Reference books (e.g., Encyclopedia, dictionaries) and thesis.

Rooms Assignment Service > FAQs


Rooms Assignment Service > What are the payment options available for housing fees?
The payment process is made electronically by logging into the university website or bank transfer, and the cash payment option is not available.

Rooms Assignment Service > Are there options available for installments or exemption from housing fees?
Housing fees are paid once before entering the housing units and cannot be paid in installments or exempted.

Rooms Assignment Service > What are the housing units for female students?
Maqam 1, Maqam 2, Maqam 3, Maqam 4, New Campus (Al Rouda).

Rooms Assignment Service > What are the housing units for male students?
Tawam, Saih bin Ammar, Maqam 5 (Al Ghadeer), Muwaiji, ZAFRAN.

Rooms Assignment Service > What are the conditions of transferring between housing units?
The student must be enrolled and continuing in the university, and he/she completed 60 credit hours (CHs) or more.

Rooms Assignment Service > When is transfer between housing units allowed?
The transfer between student housing units opens before the beginning of each semester.

Rooms Assignment Service > How can we use medical reports to transfer to other housing units or a private room?
Submit a recent medical report issued by a government hospital or an approved specialist. The report must not be older than one month from the application submission date. Medical reports and supporting documents will be reviewed by the specialized Medical Committee, which meets every Thursday to evaluate cases and issue appropriate recommendations. 6. Degree Completion and Graduation

Overview
Covers policies and procedures relating to the requirements for, confirmation of, and awarding
of academic degrees including: undergraduate degrees, structure of undergraduate degree
programs,  limits  on  transfer  credits  for          undergraduate  degrees,  application  for  degree,
certification of degree completion, graduation standing, and graduation honors.

Scope
Applies to all students and all academic and related administrative units of the University except
those in the College of Medicine and Health Sciences.

Objective
Ensures that the confirmation of completion and awarding of academic degrees functions of the
University is conducted in a manner that is consistent with academic principles, standards, and
expectations of the University appropriate to its educational mission and academic programs,
and operate with necessary integrity, fairness, consistency, and effectiveness.

Policy
1.  Undergraduate degree programs at UAEU will be reflective of the prevailing content,
    academic expectations, and learning outcomes of corresponding academic programs at
    internationally recognized public universities.
2.  The University will provide distinctive and high quality undergraduate degree programs by
    adopting    common academic requirements applicable to all students across the colleges,
    recognizing the educational needs and expectations of the nation in program creation and
    operation, and designing and conducting undergraduate degree programs to meet college or
    program-level international accreditation standards or equivalent recognition.
3.  The  University  will  recognize  outstanding  academic  achievement  through                        a  special
    designation at graduation.

Procedures of Policy No. (6) - Degree Completion and Graduation

1. Undergraduate Degrees
    A Bachelor’s Degree may be awarded only to students who have satisfied minimum credit
    hour  and  Grade  Point  Average  requirements  and  other  established  degree-specific
    requirements based on all applicable University Policies and Procedures.
    a)   The minimum number of earned credit hours required for a Bachelor’s Degree is (120).
         The minimum number of credit hours required for a student who transfers among UAEU
         Colleges may be higher than (120).
    b)   The number of earned credit hours required for a Bachelor’s Degree is dependent on the
         student’s program of study.
    c)   The minimum Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) required for a Bachelor’s
         Degree is (2.00).
    d)   No student may be awarded a Bachelor’s Degree with a grade of “I” (Incomplete) on
         his/her academic record.
    e)   Upon the recommendation of the academic advisor and approval of the College Dean,
         a student may be allowed to register for additional courses in his/her College if he/she
         needs to raise the CGPA to the minimum required for graduation.


2. Structure of Undergraduate Degree Programs
    a)   Bachelor’s    Degree programs vary by College and may include, to different degrees,
         five specific components, each with a defined minimum number of credit hours, specific
         courses, and/or demonstrated proficiency.
         1)     General Education/Core Curriculum Requirements – The Core Curriculum is a
                University-wide  requirement  of  General  Education  courses  and  proficiencies
                applicable to all students.
         2)     College-wide Requirements – College requirements apply to all students in the
                specific college, and may vary depending on the student’s major field of study.
         3)     Major/Specialization Requirements – Major requirements apply to the student’s
                specific area of specialization including minors and concentrations, and may vary
                depending on the student’s major field of study.
         4)     Elective Courses – “Free Electives” are courses a student may take in or outside
                his/her College to complete his/her degree requirements.
         5)     A college    may propose one or more minors at their programs,                  which must      be
                reviewed and approved through University Procedures.
         6)     A student may apply to the College Dean to include an approved minor in his/her
                academic plan.
         7)     Some Colleges may require students to meet the Exit Proficiency requirements.
                Exit Proficiencies may be met by passing a relevant proficiency examination in
                addition to, or in lieu of, credit courses.
    b)   Students whose academic qualifications on entering the University are insufficient to
         qualify for registration in degree-credit courses will be required to demonstrate relevant
         proficiencies  and/or  complete  appropriate  Foundation  or  remedial  courses  as  a
         prerequisite to register in degree-credit University courses.

3. Limits on Transfer Credits – Undergraduate Degrees
    a)   Only    courses    from  institutions      approved  by  the      Ministry  of  Education  may  be
         transferred to UAEU for degree credit.
    b)   For UAEU Colleges and/or degree programs with specialized international accreditation
         or the equivalent, core courses (those courses required in the major/specialization of the
         College)  may  be  transferred  to  UAEU  for  degree  credit  and  applied  to  degree
         requirements only when taken at institutions holding identical or equivalent specialized
         international accreditation. The Dean of the receiving College may make exceptions to
         this limitation on a case-by-case basis.
    c)   A student transferring from another institution must complete at least (75%) of the total
         credit hours required for the degree, and all senior-level courses in the academic major,
         at UAEU.
    d)   Determination of the applicability of transfer credit to the requirements of a specific
         undergraduate degree is the exclusive decision of the College.
    e)   Acceptance of credits earned at other institutions subsequent to the student’s initial
         enrollment at UAEU must have the prior approval of the student’s College.
    f)   Only courses in which the final grade was (C-) or better will be considered for transfer
         credit.


4. Application for Degree
    An undergraduate student  expecting to complete his  or her degree requirements  and
    graduate in a given academic semester must submit the appropriate application to his/her
    College Advising Unit and to the Office of the Admission and Registration Deanship no
    later than the last day to drop a course without failure for the academic semester.


5. Certification of Degree Completion
    a)   The student’s Academic College confirms completion of degree requirements for all
         Bachelor’s Degrees.
    b)   Subject to confirmation in the University’s official Student Information System, the
         Office of the     Admission and Registration           Deanship     certifies degree completion and
         degree awards.
    c)   Degrees are awarded at the end of each academic semester – fall, spring, and summer semesters.
    d)   The official date of a degree award is the final day of the academic semester as specified
         in the Academic Calendar, regardless of the date when the degree is certified.


6. Graduation Standing
    The academic performance of Bachelor’s                  Degree recipients may be characterized for
    summary “Graduation Standing” as follows:
    a)   Excellent – CGPA of 3.60 to 4.00
    b)   Very Good – CGPA of 3.00 to 3.59
    c)   Good – CGPA of 2.50 to 2.99
    d)   Passing – CGPA of 2.00 to 2.49

    a)   The  University  recognizes  two  levels  of  outstanding  academic  achievements                          for

         1)   First Class Honors – CGPA of 4.00
         2)   Second Class Honors – CGPA of at least 3.60
    b)   To qualify for Graduation Honors, a student must have completed at least 75% of his or
         her degree credits at UAEU.
    c)   A student who failed a course calculated towards his CGPA  (F, FA and) will not qualify
         for graduation with honors.

تجربة الحرم الجامعي
توفر جامعة الإمارات العربية المتحدة أفضل المرافق والخبرة في فئتها للطلاب. يقع الحرم الجامعي في أكثر إمارات الإمارات العربية المتحدة هدوءًا وهدوءًا ، وهي العين. تقع الجامعة في بيئة توفر النمو الشامل للطالب من جميع وجهات النظر مثل الأكاديمية والمهنية والصحة مع بيئة التعلم والنمو الصحيحة.

إكتشف أكثر

خدمات
تم تجهيز الحرم الجامعي بالمرافق التي يحتاجها الفرد لحياته السعيدة والصحية في الجامعة. نوادي الطلاب ، النادي الصحي ، الأنشطة الطلابية ، المطاعم ومنافذ البيع بالتجزئة هي بعض منها لإدراجها في القائمة. تم اختيار الموظفين وتدريبهم بعناية لإنشاء ودعم بيئات معيشية ترحيبية وشاملة تساعد الطلاب على المساعي الأكاديمية والشخصية والاجتماعية.

إكتشف أكثر

يدعم
يقوم قسم خدمات الطلاب بتطوير وتنسيق وتقديم خدمات دعم شاملة بناءً على نهج شخصي لنمو طلابنا وتطورهم من خلال تقديم خدمات التصميم والخدمات الصحية وخدمات الاستشارة وخدمات الطلاب الدوليين وخدمات المساعدة المالية وغيرها الكثير.

إكتشف أكثر

اكتشف العين


اكتشف العين > مكان رائع
العين هي واحدة من أكثر الإمارات هدوءًا في الإمارات العربية المتحدة وتتمتع بسمعة طيبة كمركز اجتماعي واقتصادي في الإمارات العربية المتحدة. مثل العديد من الجامعات العالمية ، تقع جامعة الإمارات العربية المتحدة في مدينة العين مع أكثر المناطق الجغرافية تميزًا بخصائص مختلفة.

كلية الحوسبة والذكاء الاصطناعي


كلية الحوسبة والذكاء الاصطناعي > حول الكلية
تعدُّ كلية الحوسبة والذكاء الاصطناعي الكلية الأحدث بجامعة الامارات العربية المتحدة، حيث أنشأت عام 2001، وقد اكتسبت سمعةً عالميةً واسعةً لتميزها في البحث العلمي والتدريس. توظف كلية الحوسبة والذكاء الاصطناعي نخبة من أعضاء هيئة التدريس من مختلف أنحاء العالم من حملة الدكتوراه المشهود لهم عالمياً بإسهاماتهم البارزة في مجال البحث العلمي، والابتكار والتعليم؛ إضافةً إلى فريق من حملة الماجستير الذين يقدمون الدعم اللازم للمختبرات العلمية وفريق من الإداريين، والتقنيين المتفانين في عملهم

هندسة الكمبيوتر

شعرت بالفخر عندما حققت حلمي في الالتحاق بقسم أمن المعلومات في جامعة الإمارات العربية المتحدة. الهدف من دراسة هذا التخصص هو تحقيق الأمن الإلكتروني في دولة الإمارات العربية المتحدة، وتأمين المعلومات من الوصول غير المصرح به من قبل أي شخص وحماية المعلومات من التلاعب أو الحذف. تخصص أمن المعلومات له أهمية كبيرة في عصرنا، حيث يستخدم معظم البشر أجهزة الكمبيوتر لحفظ المستندات الشخصية والمعلومات الخاصة، مما يجعل كلية الحوسبة والذكاء الاصطناعي تزود الطلاب بكل الوسائل لصقل مهاراتهم، بما في ذلك الدورات المجانية والمشاريع العلمية والمسابقات، وتسعى إلى توفير نظام عالي السرية يهدف بشكل أساسي إلى مواصلة عملية الحماية والتأمين في جميع الأوقات.

أمن المعلومات

تعتبر دراسة هندسة الكمبيوتر في جامعة الإمارات العربية المتحدة فرصة رائعة لاكتساب المعرفة والتعلم من المتخصصين. يتناول هذا التخصص تصميم وإنشاء أنظمة برمجية عالية الفعالية والقدرة على تلبية احتياجات العملاء. يسعى هذا التخصص إلى الجمع بين المبادئ الرياضية وعلوم الكمبيوتر وقواعد الهندسة الكهربائية العملية من خلال التطبيق العملي والتجارب المتعمقة في أصول التخصص. حيث يعد علم هندسة الكمبيوتر الاستثمار الحقيقي لبناء جيل واعد.

أنا سعيدة جدًا كوني طالبة هندسة كمبيوتر في جامعة الإمارات العربية المتحدة. يسلط هذا البرنامج الضوء على البرمجيات والأجهزة، بالإضافة إلى علم الشبكات ووسائل الاتصال. تتنوع برامج كلية الحوسبة والذكاء الاصطناعي في الجامعة، ويتوفر للطلاب العديد من الفرص التي تدعم مهاراتهم وتمكنهم من المشاركة في العديد من المشاريع والأبحاث، بالإضافة إلى المسابقات والمعارض التي تفتح لهم آفاقًا جديدة للتعاون مع كبرى الشركات والمستثمرين في مجال التكنولوجيا.
